strategy.summary: Reproduce SciPy special-function accuracy failure in `scipy.special.ncfdtr` (and equivalently `scipy.stats.ncf.cdf`) using the parameter set that triggers the known discrepancy; run the exact special test added in the PR so it fails on the buggy revision (cdflib inversion + Boost wrapper mismatch) and passes on the fixed revision.

build_commands: python3.6 -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
python3.6 -m pip install numpy==1.13.3 cython pytest mpmath
pinned_because: NumPy pinned to 1.13.3 per documented constraint in issue context (numerically relevant).
Python pinned to 3.6.3 (final) per documented environment in issue context.

strategy.reproducing_test: test_ncfdtr in `scipy/special/tests/test_cdflib.py` added by PR#21505 (parameterized exact reference values, `rtol=1e-13`).
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy SciPy revision `28709e534336`, running `test_ncfdtr` fails its `assert_allclose(sp.ncfdtr(dfn, dfd, nc, f), expected, rtol=1e-13, atol=0)` for at least one of the listed parameter tuples (notably the known one `dfn=6, dfd=33, nc=30.4, f=20` corresponds to the accuracy problem). After checking out the fixed revision from PR#21505, the same `pytest` target passes (all tuples match the stored high-precision references within `1e-13` relative tolerance).
strategy.numerical_probe: `scipy.special.ncfdtr(dfn, dfd, nc, f)` as exercised via `test_ncfdtr`’s exact input grid; classification is binary by the test’s `assert_allclose` (no manual numeric inspection required).
risks: Toolchain/build must be reproducible: SciPy builds C/Fortran and its special-function implementation may depend on compiler flags and availability of Boost; if Boost linkage differs, the accuracy behavior and this test’s failure/pass transition may not occur.

The provided evidence does not specify whether float32/float64 or vectorization impacts the discrepancy; the test uses Python floats (float64) and should be consistent, but reproductions on unusual BLAS/NumPy builds could differ slightly.
No documented matplotlib version constraint is provided; this strategy does not rely on importing matplotlib.

If the fixed PR changes the implementation under different build backends (e.g., OpenMP/threading settings), the failure mode may not reproduce; keep default SciPy build flags unless your CI requires overrides.
Platform/architecture is unspecified; if the defect is architecture-specific, this transition may only occur on the same CPU/OS family used in the report.

oracle.reference_source: Hard-coded expected values generated by mpmath at mp.dps=100 (script described in the test comment), matching formula 26.2.20 with `betainc(..., regularized=True)` and `nsum` over j.
oracle.why: The added regression test compares SciPy’s `sp.ncfdtr` against stored high-precision references; the buggy revision disagrees enough to violate `assert_allclose` at rtol=1e-13.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: `test_ncfdtr` fails because `scipy.special.ncfdtr` on the buggy revision returns values with accuracy error versus the stored high-precision expected results (known example: 0.998868 vs expected 0.998921 for (6,33,30.4,20)); therefore `assert_allclose(..., rtol=1e-13, atol=0)` triggers an assertion failure.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: After applying PR#21505’s fix (Boost-based wrapper accuracy + consistent inversion/implementation path), `scipy.special.ncfdtr` matches the stored mpmath references for all parameter tuples in `test_ncfdtr`, so the same `pytest` target passes.
